title: Operator decision tree for variant fallbacks - UX walkthrough
content:
Purpose:
- Capture a compact, operator-focused decision-tree UI concept for configuring automatic fallbacks and resilience during canary/A-B rollouts.
- Provide concrete wireframe notes, microcopy candidates, and backlog tickets for prototyping the editor in Console v2.

Context / problem statement:
- Operators need an expressive but safe way to encode fallback policies that fire when one or more probes/metrics cross thresholds during progressive rollouts.
- Current console UIs expose separate toggles (auto-fallback, retry), but lack a single place to visualize causal paths: trigger -> check -> action.
- Goal: reduce cognitive load for on-call and release operators while preventing accidental broad failovers.

Primary personas:
1) Release engineer (on-call) running canary -> needs quick rollback/route fallback with minimal config.
2) Platform operator setting default fallback guardrails for tenant teams.
3) Product manager reviewing rollout policies during release planning.

User stories (priority ordered):
- As a release engineer, I want to view the fallback decision tree for a rollout at a glance so I can understand what will happen if a probe fails.
- As a platform operator, I want to restrict which actions are possible for service accounts (e.g., no full-rollback) so large teams can't cause outages accidentally.
- As a PM, I want to simulate a metric breach and see which action would have been executed.

Design concept (high level):
- Single-pane "Fallback Editor" attached to a rollout policy. Top row: named policy + last modified by + quick toggle (enabled/disabled).
- Middle: visual decision canvas showing nodes: Trigger -> Condition(s) -> Actions. Nodes collapsed by default; hover to expand details.
- Right rail: contextual help & simulated run button ("Run dry simulation") + quick links to logs and related alerts.
- Bottom: a compact audit preview listing the exact operations that will be executed when action fires (e.g., "Shift 20% traffic to stable-model-v3, notify #releases, create rollback issue").

Microcopy examples (candidates):
- Policy name placeholder: "e.g., degrade-to-stable-on-latency-spike"
- Trigger label: "When probe fails" (tooltip: "Probes are checks configured in Observability — latency p95, error rate, payload correctness tests")
- Action label: "Route to fallback variant" (tooltip: "Move traffic or switch model variant; can be immediate or gradual")
- Safety toggle copy: "Require operator approval for full rollback"

Trigger types (set to mix-and-match in editor):
- Metric threshold (p95 latency, error rate percent)
- Percent of requests failing schema validation
- Canary health probe failure count over window
- Custom webhook / external alert (Slack/Prometheus)

Condition composition UI notes:
- Allow boolean composition (AND / OR) with small chips. Default: single condition to reduce complexity.
- Visual hinting for relative severity (color band: info -> warn -> critical).
- Provide quick presets: "soft-fallback" (route 10% away), "aggressive-fallback" (route 100%), "buffered-fallback" (route to canary stable copy + notify).

Actions and safety levels:
- Actions: route-traffic, scale-down-canary, pause-rollout, full-rollback, degrade-to-lower-cost-quantized-model, notify (channels), create-ticket.
- Ability to tag an action with "requires-approval". Editor enforces at least one reviewer if tagged.

Simulation flow (right-rail):
1) Select time window and select sample traffic (canary percent).
2) Click "Run dry simulation" -> outputs expected traffic shifts and operations; shows potential side-effects (e.g., cost delta).
3) "View audit ops" expands bottom panel with step-by-step operations.

Wireframe notes (for front-end team):
- Canvas inherits per-rollout theme color; nodes are 280px wide when expanded on desktop, responsive to stack vertically on narrow screens.
- Node compact state shows 1 line summary + severity pill.
- Drag-and-drop to reorder actions, but any destructive action (full-rollback) shows confirmation modal when saved.
- Keyboard shortcuts: C to create new trigger node, A to add action, S to simulate.

Accessibility & error prevention:
- Require explicit matching of condition unit (e.g., "error_rate > 5% in 5m"). Provide unit dropdown to prevent silent misconfigurations.
- Save-and-validate step runs a lightweight check against deployed model variants (e.g., ensure fallback model exists in same region).

Backlog items (rough tickets, JIRA-style):
- RI-901: Fallback Editor - basic canvas, create/edit nodes (sprint 12)
- RI-902: Simulation engine - integrate with trace replay to estimate route shifts (spike tech debt)
- RI-903: Authorization checks - require reviewer for destructive actions (policy + UI)
- RI-904: Preset library - implement 3 default presets and allow team presets
- RI-905: Audit log integration - show who toggled fallback and exact ops executed

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Operator can create 1 trigger -> 1 condition -> 1 action policy and attach to a rollout.
- Simulation runs (dry) and returns a deterministic list of ops with a confidence estimate.
- Editor validates that action targets exist and surfaces errors inline.

Risks & unknowns (open questions):
- How heavy should the simulation be? Full trace replay vs heuristics. Performance implications.
- Which roles should be able to create "automatic full rollback"? Need to align with RBAC.
- Alerting integration surface: do we allow arbitrary webhook attachments or only pre-approved channels?

Notes-to-self / quick thoughts:
- Consider a compact YAML export/import for SREs who manage policies in Git.
- Could reuse parts of the experiment editor UI but need stricter safety gating.
- UX experiment: show "what changed" diff when policy updated and automatically pin last 3 versions in the rollout timeline.

Next steps (near-term):
- Proto sketch: Marcus to produce low-fi canvas (due 2025-01-21).
- Tech spike: SRE/infra to prototype lightweight simulation stubs (due 2025-01-28).
- Design review: bring to weekly Product crit on 2025-01-30.

Slack refs / links:
- design thread: #prod-console (Slack link omitted)
- incident example: INC-2024-11-higher-latency (see linked_artifacts)

Open required decisions for triage:
- Default preset semantics (soft vs aggressive)
- Whether simulation is required before enabling an automated fallback (safety default: require simulation run once)
